why: phase-427 W4 — `nros::Node` PLUS an inline pool of N `nros::Timer` slots, and the answer to what became of `ComponentNode`'s `Timer timers_[NROS_COMPONENT_MAX_TIMERS]`. A `Timer`'s destructor cancels its timer, so one created in a constructor must outlive the call; the pool is what let a component write `create_wall_timer_in<C, &C::tick>(500)` with no storage argument. Merging that pool onto `Node` would have charged every node in the tree 192 unconditional bytes for storage most never touch, on targets chosen for having no memory to spare — so the depth is a TEMPLATE PARAMETER and the default is zero: plain `Node` carries no pool and `sizeof(Node)` is unchanged by this half of the merge. Upstream has nothing here because `rclcpp::Node::create_wall_timer` returns a `shared_ptr` the caller owns; ours cannot allocate. It is NOT a second node type — it adds storage and two verbs, declares no identity, and every instance IS-A `Node`, which is exactly the relation `ComponentNode` never had. `Node` itself could not become the template: `rclcpp::Node` is an alias asserted by `std::is_same`, 218 in-tree sites spell `Node` with no argument list, and every `Node&` parameter in the tree would otherwise accept only one depth.
